description: Dependency updates for this repository (Cargo, npm, GitHub Actions, Swift packages, XcodeGen packages).
Ordinary updates wait 2 days after a release and come grouped by ecosystem. For Cargo and npm an update whose registry gives no release time waits to be offered, instead of skipping the wait.

Only what does not reach the shipped node, the web client, or the release builds merges by itself when CI is green: dev-only npm packages that only test and check (not the ones that build the page) and the GitHub Actions that only the CI workflows use, patch and minor, each in a group of its own. Every other update, and the weekly lock file refresh, is a pull request for a person to read.
A security fix skips the wait and is labeled security, but a person reads it before it merges; none merges by itself.
Every GitHub Action stays pinned to a commit SHA with its tag in a comment. A branch is rebased when it falls behind main, so an up-to-date rule does not leave it behind.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions that only CI uses: patch, minor, and pin updates merge when CI is green. A digest update (a tag that moved to another commit) is never merged by itself. The ones a release workflow uses are in a rule below.
Production npm packages (the page imports them): patch and minor updates in one pull request for a person.

Dev-only npm packages that only test and check (vitest, jsdom, the testing libraries, Playwright, the type packages): patch and minor merge when CI is green, in a group of their own so a production update does not hold them back. The page does not import them.
vite and its React plugin are dev-only by type but write the page that signs with the device keys: a person reads their updates, in a group of their own.
A Rust crate before 1.0 may break its interface with a minor release (and several of ours do cryptography): its minor updates are for a person, one pull request each.
A major update is a pull request for a person to read and merge.
This action is pinned to the head of a branch, which has no release date to wait for and no version to read: a person merges its updates.

Only crates.io and npm are held back for a release time they do not give: a Swift package or an action pinned to a branch comes from git tags and digests, which may give none, and would never be offered.
The GitHub Actions that the release workflows use run with the release's permissions and build what people install: a person reads their updates, as one pull request.
